name: veh_speed_MON_128
comment: EGAS-L2 MONITOR ego speed, 1/128 km/h (= veh_speed_FUNC_100 * 32/25). All L2 monitor speed compares are cal_u8_kmh * 0x80 (=*128). NOTE: not every '* 0x80' in these monitors is a speed compare - torque/accel values are also scaled *0x40/*0x80.

name: veh_speed_FUNC_100
comment: FUNCTIONAL ego speed (core ctx0), 0.01 km/h. The functional ACC path uses this; the L2 monitors use veh_speed_MON_128 instead.

name: veh_speed_FUNC_100_ctx1
comment: Functional ego speed, core ctx1 twin of veh_speed_FUNC_100 (0.01 km/h).

name: cru_acc_active_flag
comment: Cruise/ACC-active operating flag (= d000abfc, written by the 0x8031 ACC/DCC state block via FUN_801915ce). GATES the #208 cruise-speed monitor: its floor/latch only runs when cruise/ACC is the active longitudinal controller. This is what makes #208 ACC-specific.

name: MON_acc_long_setpoint
comment: Monitor-domain copy of the cruise/ACC longitudinal setpoint (LSB x0x40), built by FUN_800e37de from the GRA/cruise setpoint block (802c4ee8 <- d0008980/84). Bounded by the #213 monitor (800f4abe) inside speed/dwell rails; shared input across the L2 monitor cluster.

name: EGAS_L2_cru_speed_monitor_A
comment: *** THE genuine ACC min-speed monitor (EGAS-L2 cruise/ACC speed-control plausibility, C_VS_MIN_CRU_MON). Gated on cru_acc_active_flag (d000a113). *** Over cal #208 @0x803896ec. Builds MON_cru_permit_flags (d000d7d1) via the persistent permit memory dc87; OPERATIVE FLOOR = 15-SET (0x80389809) / 7-CLEAR (0x8038980e) -> bit7. BEHAVIOUR: SELF-RECOVERING speed-gated PERMIT -- below the floor with dc87=0 the permit is withheld (ECU does not apply the ACC command), and it re-arms/resumes the moment speed>15 (MED17 openpilot user sees re-enable at ~15 = the SET edge). NOT a key-off-on lockout (that is the Simos); #208 feeds NONE of the torque-limp aggregator bytes and the corpus has no NV/Dem store. d00148be is only the monitor-ENGAGED latch. Fix: set both floor cells to 0.

name: EGAS_L2_cru_speed_monitor_B
comment: Continuation/second pass of EGAS_L2_cru_speed_monitor_A over the same cal #208 (Ghidra-split; enters on live registers). Re-derives the 15/7 floor into MON_cru_permit_flags bit7; shares latch d00148be + counters d00148bf/d000d822.

name: MON_cru_speed_engaged_latch
comment: #208 cruise-speed-monitor ENGAGED latch (NOT the fault). Set 800f006c:793 when cru_acc_active_flag(d000a113) AND d000d7f2 (which includes permit-bit7-SET = *permitted*); CLEARED on cruise-off (a113=0) or recovery (d240==8). Monitor-active state, not a stored fault; all volatile RAM. Below the floor the permit is simply withheld (self-recovering, re-arms at speed>15) -- no key-off-on lockout on MED17 (that was the Simos). Exported as EGAS_mon_diag_status bit0x10 (a per-cycle mirror, zero internal readers).

name: EGAS_mon_diag_status
comment: Shared per-monitor diagnostic status bitfield (Dem status projection). bit0x10 (b4) = a per-cycle MIRROR of MON_cru_speed_engaged_latch (via getter 802184f2) = 'cru-speed monitor engaged', NOT a stored fault. Has ZERO internal readers; the ACC/ESP coordinator 801455ae reads only bits 0x40/0x04. NOT a stored fault: the corpus has no NV/Dem write for this bit, and #208's effect is a self-recovering permit withhold (re-arms at speed>15), not a lockout. The key-off-on hard lockout was the Simos, not MED17.

name: MON_cru_permit_floor_flag
comment: L2 monitor PERSISTENT permit memory: 'vehicle has been in the cruise-speed range'. SET when veh_speed_MON_128 > 15 (0x80389809); CLEARED when speed < 7 (0x8038980e); HOLDS between. Written ONLY in the floor block (800f006c:742 / 800f027c:656), reset NOWHERE -> persists across latch cycles + ACC on/off (zeroed only at key-on). Updated only while the monitor is un-latched (arming phase). -> MON_cru_permit_flags bit7; on the next cycle it arms MON_cru_speed_engaged_latch. The 15 = arm-from-scratch, the 7 = re-arm floor (both live).

name: MON_cru_permit_flags
comment: #208 monitor's private cru-permit bitfield (referenced only in 800f006c/027c). bit7 = MON_cru_permit_floor_flag (15/7). The L2 half of the L1/L2 speed-control plausibility; feeds the d00148be latch, not the ACC control path directly.

name: MON_speed_above17_flag
comment: #208 companion band: SET when veh_speed_MON_128 > C_VS_MON_speed17_SET (0x8038980a=17); CLEARED below 17 - C_VS_MON_speed17_bandwidth2(0x80389808=2) = 15. -> d000d7de. SECONDARY arming window (not the operative floor).

name: MON_speed_17band_state
comment: Latched output of MON_speed_above17_flag (17/15). Secondary arming window for other #208 sub-checks; also read by #213 (800f4abe).

name: C_VS_MON_CRU_permit_SET_15
comment: cal #208 +0x11d, u8 km/h = 15. *** THE operative ACC min-speed lever -- the SET/ARM edge. *** EGAS_L2_cru_speed_monitor_A:737 veh_speed_MON_128 > 15*128 -> permit bit7=1 -> the engaged-latch ARMS. The 15/7 floor block runs ONLY while the latch=0 (:728); once armed it holds until ACC-off. The permit memory dc87 is persistent (never reset); with dc87=0 (fresh key-on below 15, or after dropping below 7) the latch never arms and the ACC command is withheld below 15. Set cal=0 -> dc87 arms at any speed>0. Set WITH CLR_7 (7->0, so dc87 never clears) for a re-engage-robust fix. Recompute cal checksum.

name: C_VS_MON_CRU_permit_CLR_7
comment: cal #208 +0x122, u8 km/h = 7. RE-ARM / memory-clear edge -- LIVE. 800f006c:742 `speed < 7*128` clears dc87 (MON_cru_permit_floor_flag), a PERSISTENT hysteretic memory (SET at 15, CLEAR at 7, written only in the floor block, reset nowhere). dc87 holds across latch/ACC cycles, so once =1 you can drop and RE-ENGAGE ACC down to 7; below 7 (un-latched) dc87 clears -> must exceed 15 to re-arm. The floor block runs only while un-latched (arming phase), so this edge is live on every (re-)engagement. Set cal=0 -> dc87 never clears. Set with SET_15.

name: C_VS_MON_speed17_SET
comment: cal #208 +0x11e, u8 km/h = 17. SET edge of the secondary 17/15 band (MON_speed_above17_flag). Clear = 17 - 0x80389808(2) = 15. SECONDARY (arms other sub-checks), not the operative floor. Move with the primary floor for L1/L2 consistency if needed.

name: C_VS_MON_speed17_bandwidth2
comment: cal #208 +0x11c, u8 km/h = 2. Hysteresis BAND WIDTH (subtracted) for the 17-band -> clear edge 15. Relative band, leave stock.

name: EGAS_L2_ACC_longsetpoint_band_213
comment: ACC-relevant (indirect) EGAS-L2 monitor of the ACC/GRA longitudinal setpoint (cal #213 @0x8038a3c8). Bounds MON_acc_long_setpoint (d000d5aa) inside speed/dwell-dependent accel/torque rails (d000d832/d834); debounced sub-faults FEED #208 (d000d829/d82a/d842 -> 800f006c) and the aggregator (d83c/d/e -> FUN_800d9936 -> d344 -> aa23 -> 0x8031 ACC/DCC ctrl). GENUINE speed edges: 0x8038a4ec(=0, moving/standstill) and 0x8038a4ed(=25, sub-check enable). The cells 0x8038a4d7/d8/d9(=16/18/16) and 0x8038a4ee(=12) are torque/accel RAIL coefficients + hysteresis, NOT speed floors..

name: EGAS_L2_cru_lowspeed_crawl_215
comment: ACC-relevant (indirect) EGAS-L2 cruise/ACC low-speed CRAWL monitor (cal #215 @0x8038a568). Fault severity d000d857 -> cruise fault-reaction manager 800dca9c (can force fault/off via d000d3fc) + aggregator 800d9936. Two-stage state machine d000d858/d859 (cases 0-3). Its crawl trip runs ONLY in the failsafe branch (when internal signal 0x3fc is STALE - runs at startup/on-message-loss, NOT proven dead). Speed cells 0x8038a5c9/ca(=6)/cd(=5) are crawl ARMING windows, 0x8038a5c6(=20) an upper counter-reset bound, 0x8038a5cb(=0) DISABLES a d859 transition. Not an ACC engage floor..

name: EGAS_L2_fault_aggregator
comment: THE EGAS-Level-2 monitor DTC/fault aggregator. AND-masks ~8-15 monitor result bytes (from 800f25e2/800f40bc/800f5d68/800f5982/800f4abe/...) with cal enables into fault dwords d000d32c/d334/d338, computes overall verdict d000d344 (0-3 severity) -> d000aa23 (read by the 0x8031 ACC/DCC controller) = the EGAS-3 torque-limitation/limp reaction. Terminal sink for all L2 monitors.

name: EGAS_L2_fault_verdict
comment: Overall EGAS-L2 fault verdict/severity (0-3) from EGAS_L2_fault_aggregator. Copied to EGAS_L2_reaction_level (d000aa23) via FUN_802c51c2; drives the engine torque-limitation/limp reaction.

name: EGAS_L2_reaction_level
comment: = EGAS_L2_fault_verdict (d000d344). Read by the 0x8031 ACC/DCC controller functions (80312f70/803147dc/80315a54, mirrored to d000abed) - the ACC-facing effect of a confirmed L2 monitor fault (torque limp).

name: EGAS_L2_torque_monitor_209_NOTACC
comment: NOT an ACC monitor - general engine-torque EGAS-L2 plausibility (Momentenueberwachung), cal #209 @0x80389868. Compares model vs permitted torque, debounces faults into d000deea/deeb -> packed df0a-0d -> EGAS_L2_fault_aggregator. Speed cells 0x8038a205/206/207 (8/5/0) are torque-check low-speed windows; 0x8038a202-204 (255/255/254) DISABLE their speed gates. No ACC coupling.

name: EGAS_L2_torque_monitor_214_NOTACC
comment: NOT an ACC monitor - general EGAS-L2 torque-vs-speed plausibility, cal #214 @0x8038a514. 0x8038a551(=10) is a low-speed SUPPRESSION term for a torque check, not an ACC floor. Latches a held verdict d000d846 -> EGAS_L2_fault_aggregator. No ACC coupling.

name: EGAS_L2_torque_plaus_seq_173_NOTACC
comment: NOT an ACC monitor - EGAS-L2 sequential torque-plausibility, cal #173 @0x80385c4c. Its 0x8038679b(=15) is the LOWER BOUND of a torque-window [15,105] arming a corridor check on MON_acc_long_setpoint - a numerical coincidence, NOT the C_VS_MIN_CRU_MON floor. All state volatile, no non-volatile latch, no ACC var referenced. Do NOT edit for openpilot.

name: EGAS_L2_channel_plaus_211_NOTACC
comment: NOT an ACC monitor - EGAS-L2 redundant channel/pedal plausibility voting, cal #211 @0x8038a25a. 0x8038a3a4(=255) is a de-facto DISABLED 255 km/h over-speed ceiling; other speed uses are axis/threshold selects. Packs df2d/2e/2f -> EGAS_L2_fault_aggregator. No ACC coupling.

name: EGAS_L2_torque_coordinator_NOTACC
comment: NOT an ACC monitor - EGAS-L2 permitted-vs-actual longitudinal torque check. Enabled only in a 25-130 km/h driving window (the opposite of a low-speed floor). Sets monitor result d000e036. No ACC coupling.

name: EGAS_L2_accel_torque_model_NOTACC
comment: NOT an ACC monitor - EGAS-L2 longitudinal accel/torque MODEL. Vehicle speed is a MAP AXIS input, not a floor. Contains the MONITOR twin of the +/-500000 decel rail (the monitor's own authority, not the functional one). Outputs d000d5xx monitor group.

name: EGAS_L2_roadload_model_NOTACC
comment: NOT an ACC monitor - EGAS-L2 road-load/driving-resistance model: v^2 aero drag + v rolling + accel terms -> resistance shadows d000dfe2/e8 (feeds EGAS_L2_torque_coordinator 800fb796). Speed used as physical model axis, not a threshold.

name: EGAS_L2_step_dtc_manager_193_NOTACC
comment: NOT an ACC monitor - EGAS-L2 operating-step sequencer + DTC manager, cal #193 @0x80387f5c. 0x80387fbc(=6) gates only the internal step-active flag d000d6f7 in coast-state (SUPPRESSES the sequencer at low speed). No ACC var referenced.

name: EGAS_L2_torque_plaus_148_NOTACC
comment: NOT an ACC monitor - EGAS-L2 monitor-domain torque plausibility, cal #148 @0x8038436a. PROVABLY produces no low-speed fault: double-gated (subsystem-state d3cd in {3,8} + operating-point>=80, then hysteresis d000d867 SET>12 / CLEAR<5 via 0x80384761=5 low-edge + 0x80384760=7 band-width) -> self-disables below ~12 km/h. Outputs feed only telemetry+getter. No ACC coupling.

name: ACC_master_state_machine
comment: ACC/GRA master state machine. Transition table @0x80044772 (134 entries): a3c1 (ACC_master_mode, out_idx 0x1b) = a DIRECT COPY of cond[0x1c] = the 2-bit commanded mode. NO engine-side speed floor gates engagement; it relays the commanded ACC mode (openpilot via ACC_01).

name: statemachine_unpack_cond_vector
comment: Unpacks the 10-byte packed ACC condition vector into 50 condition slots (1-3 bits each). cond[0x1c]=byte5[5:6]=the 2-bit ACC mode -> ACC_master_mode.

name: statemachine_confirm_transition
comment: Transition-confirm layer over ACC_cond_vec_current (d0009b63) vs _new (d0009b70) via descriptor 0x8003f374. Event-driven; no speed compare.

name: statemachine_load_cond_vec_coding
comment: Loads the ACC engage-condition vector from the CODING data store, not from an event mailbox. FUN_8008ebbc(&UNK_d0009b48,&d000b9ad,0xe,0,0x34) reads a 52-byte record from store class 0xe (a coding/config store: sibling reads use records 0x14/0x16/0x1b/0x33 with sizes 1-10 and each has a flash fallback). The other branch copies the flash coding default DAT_803def94 into ACC_cond_vec_current/_new. So a3c1 (ACC master mode) is CODING-determined, not event-driven; there is no runtime condition-event producer to find. FUN_8008ebbc posts a request into the 8-slot service ring at d0006a10 and spins on FUN_8008f464 until serviced -- it is a synchronous store read, not an async mailbox.

name: ACC_cond_vec_current
comment: Current packed ACC engage-condition vector (10 bytes). byte5[5:6] = commanded ACC mode -> ACC_master_mode.

name: ACC_cond_vec_new
comment: Candidate/new packed ACC engage-condition vector; confirmed into ACC_cond_vec_current.

name: ACC_master_mode
comment: ACC/GRA master mode: 0=inactive,1=GRA,2=ACC,3=ACC-extended = direct copy of engage condition slot 0x1c. Feeds d000a454 via FUN_802c806e. No engine-side speed floor gates this.

name: ACC_status_rx
comment: RX-side ACC status index, unpacked by FUN_800b1136 from ACC_01 (0x109) bit 60 len 3 = ACC_Status_ACC. PROVEN from the COM signal-descriptor table (record @0x80038ad8, desc 0x0000033c), not inferred; corroborated by on-car CAN where openpilot's commanded status maps 1:1 through tbl[] to TSK_04. A second descriptor @0x80038a60 binds the same byte from bit 57 len 3 (platform variant). -> a368 via FUN_800b0e94.

name: ACC_state_a368
comment: ACC state enum (0=off 1=engaged 2=engaged+override 3=fault). Sole writer FUN_800b0e94: a368 = tbl[ACC_status_rx], tbl_A@0x8004579a=[0,0,2,1,1,0,2,3] (selectors 0x55/0x73), tbl_B@0x800457a2=[0,0,0,1,2,0,0,3] (selectors 0x2a/0x56); selector 0x29 uses d000a5a4 directly. Copied to ab01 by FUN_801455ae.

name: TSK04_status_ab01
comment: Source shadow for TSK_04 (0x10E) TSK_Status_GRA_ACC_02 (62|2). = ACC_state_a368, forced to 3 when the present-gate word is nonzero, and forced to 0 by the FUN_801455ae suppressor (ab01 in {1,2} AND d0000121 bit5, zero debounce -- cal #251 +0xc/+0xe are both 0). Case 0 rails the request outputs: d0005f20 = d0005d00 = -500000. *** INCOMPLETE. *** This describes only FUN_801455ae's LONG branch, which is DEAD CODE on this calibration: 0x801455b6/bc test cal_obj(a9+0x3ec)=0x803b5230 bytes [0x21] and [0x24], both 0, so the SHORT branch is taken unconditionally and 0x801455e4/ee does d000ab01 = d000a350. TSK_04's status is a direct copy of d0004936.

name: GE_Waehlhebel_rx
comment: Gear SELECTOR LEVER position, from Getriebe_03 (0x102) bit 44 len 4 = GE_Waehlhebel. PROVEN: COM descriptor record @0x80039c08 (desc 0x42c) sits in the Getriebe_03 PDU group @0x80039be0 (75% DBC geometry match), and the on-car log shows the P->R->N->D sequence 5->6->7->8 at drive start and the reverse at drive end. NOT a cruise state -- an earlier label (cru_state_rx) was wrong. Read only by FUN_80087a70.

name: gear_sel_state
comment: Mapped gear-selector state = tbl[GE_Waehlhebel_rx] (FUN_80087a70, sole writer). tbl@0x800453b4 = identity[0..14] when (d0008c80 & 0x610)==0 && (d0008c80 & 0x1000)==0, else tbl@0x80045395 = [0,0,0,0,0,8,7,6,5,12,17,0,0,14,14]. States {6,8} = selector in R or D (FUN_80087a70 computes that same test at its tail). Shadowed to d0009f76 for the L2 monitor.

name: gear_sel_state_MON
comment: L2-monitor shadow copy of gear_sel_state (802c4942:155 / 802c4ee8:28). Classified by FUN_8010295e(cal#208+0x49,+0x36,.) whose LUT @0x80389735 is an IDENTITY map over 0..17, so monitor state == gear_sel_state. Feeds d7ed = debounce(state==6) and d7f1 = debounce(state==8) -- i.e. selector in R / in D.

name: MON_cru_active_permit
comment: #208 suppression term holding d7f9 low during normal engaged driving. With cfg word cal#208+0x148 = 0x1bf3 (@0x80389834) collapsing terms 1-2 to always-true: dc8b = cru_acc_active_flag(a113) && d000d240<=8 && d000a0a9 && (gear_sel_state == 6 || == 8), i.e. GEAR SELECTOR IN R OR D. Copied to d7f6 one cycle later. NOTE: the selector was constant at D across the whole on-car log, so this term cannot explain the ~15 km/h ACC drop.

name: MON_cru_floor_fault
comment: #208's output into the EGAS-L2 fault aggregator (written 800f006c:728, read 800d9936:71). Set when d240==8 AND the d00148bf counter < cal#208+0xec AND MON_cru_permit_flags bit7 is CLEAR (below the 15 km/h floor / unarmed) AND d7f6==0. This is the path by which the min-speed monitor reaches the ACC command: d7f9 -> aggregator -> EGAS_L2_fault_verdict -> EGAS_L2_reaction_level -> the 0x8031 ACC/DCC controller.

name: ACC_Sollbeschleunigung_rx
comment: ACC_01 (0x109) bit 24 len 11 = ACC_Sollbeschleunigung -- the COMMANDED ACCEL entry point into the ECU. PROVEN from the COM signal-descriptor table: record @0x80038ba0 (desc 0x0003_0b18) inside the contiguous ACC_01 RX group @0x80038ad8..0x80038bc8 (stride 0x28, descending bit order). Written by the RX unpacker FUN_800b1136 and by the timeout-substitution setter FUN_8008b17c. -> d000830a.

name: ACC_zul_Regelabw_unten_rx
comment: ACC_01 (0x109) bit 16 len 6 = ACC_zul_Regelabw_unten. COM descriptor record @0x80038bc8, ACC_01 RX group. -> d000830c via FUN_800b1136.

name: ACC_zul_Regelabw_oben_rx
comment: ACC_01 (0x109) bit 35 len 5 = ACC_zul_Regelabw_oben. COM descriptor record @0x80038b78, ACC_01 RX group. -> d000830e via FUN_800b1136.

name: ACC_neg_Sollbeschl_Grad_rx
comment: ACC_01 (0x109) bit 40 len 8 = ACC_neg_Sollbeschl_Grad (negative jerk limit). COM descriptor record @0x80038b50. -> d0008310 via FUN_800b1136, with a '< 4 -> use default' floor.

name: ACC_pos_Sollbeschl_Grad_rx
comment: ACC_01 (0x109) bit 48 len 8 = ACC_pos_Sollbeschl_Grad (positive jerk limit). COM descriptor record @0x80038b28. -> d0008312 via FUN_800b1136, with a '< 4 -> use default' floor.

name: ACC_Dynamik_rx
comment: ACC_01 (0x109) bit 58 len 2 = ACC_Dynamik. COM descriptor record @0x80038b00, ACC_01 RX group. Read by FUN_800b0e94.

name: ACC_cmd_accel
comment: The commanded accel inside the ECU = ACC_Sollbeschleunigung after RX unpack (FUN_800b1136 selector 0x55). Validity is gated there: d00001af bit6 SET iff ACC_status_rx in {3,4}, else d0000159 bit2 (substitute). Sole reader FUN_80140922, which copies it UNCLAMPED to d00082ae.

name: TSK_cmd_accel_shadow
comment: Commanded accel handed to the TSK path: FUN_80140922 (gated d000a454==2) copies d000830a here with NO clamp. Read by FUN_801418ea, which clamps it into a speed-indexed envelope -> d00082c4.

name: TSK_accel_clamped
comment: Commanded accel after the FUN_801418ea envelope clamp: d00082c4 = max(limit_B, min(limit_A, d00082ae)) where BOTH limits are speed-indexed curve lookups over cal #247 (0x803b4834). MEASURED FLAT on this image: lower -3.0 m/s^2, upper +2.0 m/s^2 at every speed -- i.e. no speed-dependent accel limiting. -> d00082b6 (TSK_04) and d00082c0 (TSK_02).

name: TSK_ax_Getriebe_tx
comment: TSK_04 (0x10E) bit 18 len 9 = TSK_ax_Getriebe. COM descriptor record @0x80039258, inside the contiguous TSK_04 group @0x80039190+k*0x28. Sole writer FUN_8014469a: substituted with cal 0x803b508a (=0, packs to wire raw 84 = +0.000 m/s^2) whenever the bVar11 gate is false. Matches the on-car neutral exactly.

name: TSK_zul_Regelabw_tx
comment: TSK_04 (0x10E) bit 12 len 6 = TSK_zul_Regelabw. COM descriptor record @0x80039280. Written by FUN_80140922 from d000830c via func_0xc0000926(x,1000,10000).

name: TSK_Wunsch_Uebersetz_tx
comment: TSK_04 (0x10E) bit 27 len 10 = TSK_Wunsch_Uebersetz (gear-ratio request). COM descriptor record @0x80039230, TSK_04 group.

name: TSK_Verzoeg_Anf_tx
comment: TSK_02 (0x10C) bit 56 len 8 = TSK_Verzoeg_Anf -- the DECEL REQUEST the engine sends to ESP. COM descriptor record @0x800392f8 (TSK_02 group with TSK_Status 16|2 and TSK_Radbremsmom 40|12). Written by FUN_801405d4: 'uVar8 = 0; if (bVar1) uVar8 = d00082c0;' -- a HARD ZERO when the gate is false, which is the measured wire raw 166 = 0.000 m/s^2. bVar1 = (a362 in {1,5}) chain, i.e. ACC actively regulating.

name: TSK_Radbremsmom_tx
comment: TSK_02 (0x10C) bit 40 len 12 = TSK_Radbremsmom (wheel-brake torque request). COM descriptor record @0x80039320, TSK_02 group.

name: TSK_amax_moeglich_tx
comment: TSK_01 (0x10A) bit 48 len 9 = TSK_amax_moeglich. COM descriptor record @0x80039d48. Stays LIVE below the ACC floor on-car (99 distinct values, 0.000..6.072 m/s^2, tracking speed) -- the engine keeps publishing capability while withholding the request.

name: ACC_lowspeed_flag_15kmh
comment: *** THE 15 km/h CONDITION. *** Populated from INTERNAL message 0x466 (handle @0x800284b6, the only copy in the image; read via the COM receive in FUN_800a5db0). Drives d000015f bit 7 (that bit has no other writer) -> d00000e0 bit 7 -> d0004985 -> debounce(cal 0x8010384c+0x5e) -> d000f82a bit 7 -> TSK_01 (0x10A) FRAME BIT 23, which on-car is SET 0..15.28 km/h, CLEAR above, transitions at 15.08/14.90/15.38/14.88 km/h and LEADS the ACC drop by one 20 ms frame. PRODUCER NOT IN THE DISASSEMBLY: its only writers are the circular per-context shadow pair with d000ab6a; no block copy covers it; not a COM descriptor target; a 649-function guarded gap-walk added no writer. DOUBLE-CONFIRMED NEGATIVE: a linear constant-propagation scan of the EFFECTIVE ADDRESS of every memory access in all 5918 functions (core/ghidra/FindEffectiveAddr.java, which closes FindRefsTo's blind spot for base+displacement stores that leave no reference on the target byte) also finds ONLY the three circular shadow writers. Caveat: that scan seeds a0/a1/a8/a9 from ecu.conf, so a producer whose base register comes from a runtime table resolves as INDEXED rather than as a hit -- the negative is 'no resolvable-EA writer', not an absolute one. ADDRESSING FORM (this is why no literal exists): a6c7 is reached as `lea aX,[a0]-0x1d59` with a0 = 0xd000c420 (the global data base from ecu.conf BASEREGS); 0xd000c420-0x1d59 = 0xd000a6c7. Known encoding: bytes d9 <(base<<4)|dest> 27 ae. A raw-image scan for ANY 32-bit instruction carrying displacement bytes 27 ae returns 9 hits: the 6 known [a0] sites, one FALSE POSITIVE at 0x80101866 (base a15=0xd0010000 -> targets d000e2a7, not a6c7), and 2 in the 0x8002xxxx constant-pool region that are data, not code. So NO undisassembled code accesses a6c7 via this form -- a third independent method agreeing with the reference-model and effective-address scans. RESIDUAL GAP: a store through a base pointing NEAR a6c7 with a non-zero store offset (e.g. lea to a6a0 then st.b [aX]0x27) would carry a DIFFERENT displacement and evade this byte scan in undisassembled code; FindEffectiveAddr covers that case but only for disassembled functions. name: DSM_init_status_arrays
comment: DSM startup/cycle routine over the event-status arrays. Fills array2 (0xd000b117) with 0x20 (bit 5 set = test not yet completed), then walks halfword path-id RANGE pairs and clears bit 5 of array2 / bits 1|6 of array1 (0xd000b083) under interrupt-disable as tests complete. Establishes that FUN_800981cc returns latched monitor state, not a live condition. *** SEMANTICS CORRECTED. This is a Sperrmatrix (lock/inhibit matrix), NOT a 'test completed' table. arr2[path] low nibble = COUNT OF ACTIVE LOCKS; bit 5 = 'lock count == 0' = path RELEASED (Freigabe), set when the decrement reaches zero and cleared on every increment (proved from FUN_800bc5d6); bit 6 = inhibit-seen-this-sweep, bit 7 = changed/skip-resync, bit 4 = restore. So FUN_800981cc(p)==0 means p is LOCKED, not 'test not completed'. FUN_80097a76 is the cyclic re-sync engine; FUN_80097fa4 is its power-on equivalent, and its table is a CUMULATIVE BOUNDARY array at 0x80043032 (1457 x u16) indexing a flat 51231-entry slot table (path ids at *(0x801037d8), bit indices at *(0x8010380c)), not range pairs. For path 275 specifically: it is locked only via DFP groups 397 and 407, and an exhaustive scan proves NEITHER IS EVER REPORTED anywhere in the image -- so path 275 is permanently RELEASED and its status cannot change at runtime.

name: DSM_restore_status_after_load

name: ram_dispatch_jump_A
comment: RAM-table dispatcher: idx = *(0xd00072e5) - 1   [a0-0x513b]; if idx < 6 then a15 = *(0xd0004980 + idx*4); ji a15. The table lives in RAM, so its targets can NEVER be resolved statically -- Ghidra records the site as a computed jump with no targets. NOTE this is also the source of the two INDEXED false positives that FindEffectiveAddr reports for any address in 0xd0000000..0xd00001ff: the addsc.a forms 0xd0000000+idx*4 but the real access adds a 0x4980 displacement, so those hits are NOT writes to the config block. *** RETRACTED. 0xd0004980 is NOT a function-pointer table. Its .data initialiser (flash 0x80008740) is 0001f07b 803cf8d5 803cfcd5 803cf2d5 803cfed5 8038ff85 -- odd-addressed words in the CAL region, not code pointers. Every writer stores scalars (TSK_status_coordinator does st.w [a0]-0x7aa0 plus st.b/st.h at +4/+8/+0xc/+0x10/+0x14), and FUN_80019c5a walks 0xd0004968 as five 0x14-byte monitor records {int*, uint*, timestamp, u16 lo, u16 hi, u8 flag} -- 0xd0004980 is record[1]+4. The index byte 0xd00072e5 has exactly ONE writer image-wide (FUN_8001e794@0x8001e7c4) and it writes 0, and `jge.u d15,#0x6` then returns, so the ji never executes at that value. Sibling table for the B variant (0xd0004cb8) is likewise TriCore instruction bytes, not pointers. Both are reached from FUN_8001f7e4, an STM-timer handler: mode-gated debug hooks, inert in production. The REAL RAM function-pointer table is 0xd0009ed0 (155 entries, 132 distinct targets), plus 0xd000a3fc/a414/a458/aa08. *** OBSOLETE: the 'INDEXED false positive on 0xd0000000..0xd00001ff' note no longer applies -- FindEffectiveAddr now attributes the hit to the real memory operand (8001e2d2 ld.a a15,[a15]0x4980 -> d0004980). Corroboration for the retraction: 0xd0004980 = 0xd0004918 + 0x68 is INSIDE the ACC status struct, and the dispatch index range 0..5 spans 0xd0004980..0xd0004994, which includes 0xd0004985 = ACC_lowspeed_flag_copy. It is reading ACC scalars, not function pointers.

name: segC_routine_called_from_TSK02
comment: Target of calla 0xc000079c at 0x80140caa in TSK02_producer. Segment 0xC is BOOT-COPIED on-chip RAM: code that lives at rest in flash and is copied to 0xc0000000 at startup, then executed there. *** CORRECTED: the earlier note here -- 'no flash->PSPR copy table is findable by literal scan' -- was wrong in its conclusion. The scan looked for 0xc000xxxx LITERALS; the tables are 4-byte-aligned (dst,src,len) records, and two exist (see 0x800402ec and 0x8000e868). *** Note 0x9d is JA and 0xed is CALLA (TriCore format B, EA = {disp24[23:20], 7'b0, disp24[19:0], 1'b0}); the 6 'degraded' functions were NOT an unmodelled opcode at all, they branched into unmapped segment 0xC and Ghidra reports unmapped memory with the same 'Bad instruction' text that DecompileAll keys on. Exactly 5 UNCONDITIONAL_JUMP refs cross from flash into segment 0xC and they are exactly those 5 flash functions; 1879 CALLA refs reach 25 distinct segment-0xC targets (a fixed-point math library) without truncating, because a call does not need the callee body. RESOLVED: segment 0xC is the CPU-LOCAL PROGRAM SCRATCHPAD (PMI), not LMU. Evidence from the image itself, not a datasheet: the MPU region table at 0x8003fa60 splits segment 0xC into c0000000-c000013f / c0000140-c000019f / c00001a0-c000039f as data (totalling exactly 0x3a0) and c00003a0-c0007fff as code -- and the code copy lands at exactly 0xc00003a0, that boundary. On TriCore, segment 12 is architecturally the PMI local code memory. This is also why tricore tc176x.pspec (modelling TC1762/TC1766) declares nothing there. Distinct from the boot-ROM targets: those are 0xAFFFF100/0xAFFFF110 (NOT 0xafff0100/0110 as first recorded), 4 calli sites in FUN_80016c08/FUN_80017076. 0xAFFF0000-0xAFFFFFFF is the Infineon on-chip BOOT ROM (mask ROM), so they are PERMANENTLY unrecoverable from any flash dump -- an exhaustive scan for a copy record with a segment-0xA destination returns 0 matches, as does one for SPRAM 0xd4000000. Scale of the segment-0xC recovery: 27 branch targets give 27 clean function prologues, behind 2140 call sites in 569 distinct flash functions (9.6% of the corpus).

name: COM_dlc_const_table
comment: *** CORRECTED: this is a DLC CONSTANT TABLE, not a callback. *** It holds the descending bytes 8,7,6,5,4,3,2,1 and each message record's +0x10 points at the entry giving that message's payload length (most point at the 8). The earlier reading -- 'shared per-message callback, identical on every record' -- came from the wrong message-table base, where this pointer landed at +0x08 and its uniformity was mistaken for a common handler. Two records use calibratable DLC bytes at 0x80382416 (=8) and 0x80382424 (=7).

name: COM_desc_callback_alt
comment: Alternate signal-descriptor conversion callback at descriptor +0x0c, used by TSK_01's 24-bit status record 0x80039460 instead of the common 0x800286c6. Keying a descriptor scan on a single callback value silently drops records that use this one -- the reason COM_DESC_CB alone under-scans the table.

name: boot_copy_table_data
comment: Boot .data initialiser table, 12-byte records in (src, dst, len) order -- note the OPPOSITE field order to 0x800402ec; a 0xffffffff record terminates. Decoded: 0x800045c0 -> 0xc0001400 len 0x80; 0x80004640 -> 0xc0001500 len 0x248; 0x80004888 -> 0xd0000ac8 len 0x9408; 0x8000dc90 -> 0xd0009ed0 len 0x270; 0x8000df00 -> 0xd000a140 len 0x968. The third entry is the 39 KB LDRAM data image and it is what explains FUN_d00098fa: 0x80004888 + (0xd00098fa - 0xd0000ac8) = 0x8000d6ba, so those bytes are INITIALISED DATA copied into RAM, not resident code -- seven functions build small-data-area pointers into that window via a0 and WRITE to it. Treat FUN_d00098fa as an artefact to reclassify, not code to decode. Also note the 0xc0001400/0xc0001500 destinations land INSIDE the 0x800402ec code alias, so segment 0xC holds code and initialised data together and a single flat alias over it is approximate for those two sub-ranges.

name: boot_copy_table_load
comment: Boot load-image copy table, 12-byte records (dst, src, len). Several records have len=0 and are no-ops (rec0/rec3/rec7); src=0xffffffff or a repeated byte pattern marks a FILL. Live records: 0xd000bfd8 <- 0x80024f90 len 0xdb0 (.data); 0xd000cd88 <- 0x80025d40 len 0x1558 (.data); 0xc00003a0 <- 0x80020098 len 0x12d0 (TriCore code run from segment 0xC); 0xf0060000 <- 0x800222e8 len 0x2ca8; 0xf0050000 <- 0x80021368 len 0xf80; fills 0xc0001670 len 0x6990, 0xf0062ca8 len 0x1358, 0xf0050f80 len 0x1080. Sources are contiguous 0x80020098..0x80027298. *** 0xF0050000 and 0xF0060000 are the TC1797 PCP2 (Peripheral Control Processor) memories: the FILLs terminate at exactly 0xf0052000 (8 KB) and 0xf0064000 (16 KB), the PCP2 memory sizes. 0xF0060000 = CMEM (code), so 0x800222e8 len 0x2ca8 (11432 bytes) is PCP MICROCODE -- a SECOND PROCESSOR's firmware, in a different instruction set that Ghidra's TriCore model can never decode. 0xF0050000 = PRAM (0xf80). This is a real, permanently bounded slice of the 'unaccounted' byte gap. (CORRECTION: an earlier revision of this row gave the table start as 0x800402ec -- that is record 4, mid-table -- and had the CMEM/PRAM roles reversed.)

name: ram_vtable_main
comment: The image's real RAM function-pointer table: 155 entries, 132 distinct targets, all in 0xd0000ac8-0xd000aaa8. It is exactly copy-record 4 of table 0x8000e868 (src 0x8000dc90, len 0x270 = 156 words), i.e. a dedicated vtable materialised at boot. Companions: 0xd000a3fc (5), 0xd000a414 (4), 0xd000a458 (4), 0xd000aa08 (8). Because the flash boot sector 0x80000000..0x80004000 is entirely zero, the crt0 that CONSUMES these tables is absent from the dump -- which is why no code references the copy tables and why emulating the copy can never work. Applying the tables statically is exact and needs no emulator.

name: boot_rom_entry_points
comment: 0xAFFFF100 / 0xAFFFF110, called via 4 calli sites in FUN_80016c08 and FUN_80017076. Infineon on-chip BOOT ROM (mask ROM) -- not present in any flash dump and not copied there by any table in the image. PERMANENTLY out of scope for static recovery; record as a hard boundary, not an open lead.

name: Kennlinie_s16
comment: Part of the segment-0xC (PSPR) library, recovered this session by mapping the boot copy table -- before that every call site here was an unmapped address and the ACC/TSK decompiles were full of holes. Layout established by reading the code, not assumed. 1-D characteristic-curve (Kennlinie) interpolation, SIGNED 16-bit: FUN(short *tbl, int x). Layout tbl[0]=n, tbl[1..n]=X breakpoints, tbl[n+1..2n]=Y values; binary search over X then linear interpolate. 286 call sites. THIS MATTERS FOR SEARCHING: a threshold in this ECU is often a curve BREAKPOINT, not a scalar compare, so scanning cal reads for a constant cannot find it -- decode the curves instead. Verified against table 0x803dcd64 (n=5, X=200/500/1000/1500/2000 = 2..20 km/h).

name: acc_lowspeed_curve_zeroed
comment: 1-D Kennlinie (see 0xc0000638) on the ACC path: n=5, X = 200/500/1000/1500/2000 = 2.00/5.00/10.00/15.00/20.00 km/h -- exactly the low-speed band -- and Y = 0/0/0/0/0. Reached from the 0x80146xxx family via PTR_DAT_801040f4+0x318. NOT DEMONSTRATED TO BE THE 15 km/h FLOOR, and recorded here so the lead is not re-chased: the alternative branch (scalar +0x32e) is ALSO 0, so both arms of the if/else yield zero and the term is inert; the value is SUBTRACTED as an offset rather than used as a limit; and 7 of the 29 ACC-reachable curves are all-zero, so a zeroed curve is unremarkable in this calibration. Consistent with a low-speed feature present but calibrated inert (cf. the B8 single-radar 30 km/h floor), which is a hypothesis, not a finding.

name: acc_lowspeed_map_neutral

name: ACC_engage_block_flags
comment: THE 15 km/h FLOOR GATE. Byte at 0xd0004918+0xb2 whose BIT 7 is the debounced low-speed flag. VERIFIED END-TO-END at instruction level (coordinator re-checked every step independently): d00000e0 bit7 -> extr.u/st.b [a12]0x6d = d0004985 (0x8014478e-96) -> ON-delay debounce against cal cal_obj(a9+0x3e8)+0x5e = 0x803b50e6 = 6 (0x80144dda) -> packer slot [a10]+0x0c, which the TSK_bool_packer slot order makes BIT 7 (0x80144e10) -> call FUN_80143a68 (0x80144e1e) -> AND with cal cal_obj(a9+0x3e8)+0x39 = 0x803b50c1 = 0xFE = 0b11111110, so bit 7 SURVIVES the mask (0x80144e2c-30) -> st.b [a12]0xb2 = d00049ca (0x80144e34). Consumed by FUN_80143b34, which is literally `lea a15,[a0]-0x7b08; ld.bu d2,[a15]0xb2; ne d2,d2,#0; ret` -- i.e. it returns (d00049ca != 0) -- and is called from EXACTLY 4 sites, all inside ACC_engage_state_machine@0x80143b8a (0x80143bd2 case 1, 0x80143fda case 3, 0x801440ca case 5, 0x80144424 default engage evaluation). While set it forces state 1 and state 5 -> state 2 and blocks both re-engage chains; the default case then calls FUN_801439fc every cycle, zeroing d0004936 and d0004941 -- a350 and a362 railed together in ONE transition, exactly the signature measured on-car (TSK_Verzoeg_Anf and TSK_ax_Getriebe going to zero in lockstep). Re-engage has NO off-delay, so the asymmetric debounce explains why drops land below 15.0 (14.93/14.90/14.88) while the flag transitions at 15.08/15.38. CAVEATS: bits 1-6 remain independent live gates (DSM 287/271, d000aa53, the 3 km/h dwell, a deviation term), and the producer of the flag itself (d000a6c7 via COM internal message handle 0x800284b6) is still NOT in the disassembly -- the consumer side is proved, the source is not. *** INERT ON THIS VEHICLE -- do not treat bit 7 as the live floor gate. The input was traced to the end: d00049ca.b7 <- debounce <- d0004985 <- d00000e0.b7 <- d000a6c7 <- d000ab6a (copied by FUN_80317ea8 @0x803181c6-d0 and two siblings) <- COM boolean descriptor rec 0x800347ac (srcBit=36). Message ownership PROVED, not inferred: message-table field +0x2c points at each message's first boolean record, and 0x800316f0 (CAN 0x101) owns records 9..27, which contains ours. On-car log: CAN 0x101 bit 36 has exactly TWO transitions in 9393 frames, both at 0.00 km/h (ignition settle and end of log), and is constant 0 across all four 15 km/h crossings. So the mechanism is real and correctly traced, but its input is dead on this car -- most likely variant-coded off. The measured floor is enforced ELSEWHERE (see 0x106 ESP_05 note). Bits 1-6 of d00049ca remain the live gates. *** MESSAGE CORRECTED: descriptor 0x800347ac belongs to ESP_05 (CAN 0x106) frame bit 36 = ESP_HDC_Standby, NOT CAN 0x101 bit 36. The on-car measurement quoted above tested the wrong bit. The INERT verdict may still stand -- ESP_HDC_Standby is 0 on both sides of the floor in the decoded frames -- but it must be re-stated against ESP_05 bit 36, not 0x101 bit 36.

name: C_ACC_lowspeed_on_delay
comment: cal_obj(a9+0x3e8)+0x5e = 6. ON-delay for the low-speed engage-block flag, in units of 10000 (the debounce at 0x80144dd2 loads 0x2710 = 10000). There is NO off-delay, which is why re-engage is immediate while the drop is delayed. **ALTERNATIVE LEVER: 6 -> 0x7FFF** makes the delay effectively never expire, so bit 7 never sets. Less surgical than the 0x803b50c1 mask but leaves the mask semantics untouched. *** INERT ON THIS VEHICLE -- do not treat bit 7 as the live floor gate. The input was traced to the end: d00049ca.b7 <- debounce <- d0004985 <- d00000e0.b7 <- d000a6c7 <- d000ab6a (copied by FUN_80317ea8 @0x803181c6-d0 and two siblings) <- COM boolean descriptor rec 0x800347ac (srcBit=36). Message ownership PROVED, not inferred: message-table field +0x2c points at each message's first boolean record, and 0x800316f0 (CAN 0x101) owns records 9..27, which contains ours. On-car log: CAN 0x101 bit 36 has exactly TWO transitions in 9393 frames, both at 0.00 km/h (ignition settle and end of log), and is constant 0 across all four 15 km/h crossings. So the mechanism is real and correctly traced, but its input is dead on this car -- most likely variant-coded off. The measured floor is enforced ELSEWHERE (see 0x106 ESP_05 note). Bits 1-6 of d00049ca remain the live gates. *** MESSAGE CORRECTED: descriptor 0x800347ac belongs to ESP_05 (CAN 0x106) frame bit 36 = ESP_HDC_Standby, NOT CAN 0x101 bit 36. The on-car measurement quoted above tested the wrong bit. The INERT verdict may still stand -- ESP_HDC_Standby is 0 on both sides of the floor in the decoded frames -- but it must be re-stated against ESP_05 bit 36, not 0x101 bit 36.

name: C_ACC_min_speed_structural
comment: cal_obj(a9+0x3e8)+0x72 = 0. A structural ACC MINIMUM-SPEED gate: compared against ego speed by `jge d0,d15` at 0x80144922. It holds ZERO, i.e. it is already fully disabled in this calibration and is NOT the source of the 15 km/h floor. Recorded so it is not mistaken for the lever.

name: CAN_0x106_ESP_05_stale_row
comment: *** SUPERSEDED -- see the 0x80031718 row, which is the correct record address. *** This row's headline claim that the ECU NEVER unpacks ESP_05 bit 33 is FALSE. It was computed with a message-table base and boolean-pointer offset that attributed every boolean binding to the wrong message (off by one record). ESP_05 bit 33 IS unpacked, by boolean descriptor 0x80034784, into 0xd000ab42 bit 5. Likewise bits 27 and 29 are bound, not absent. Kept only so the wrong address does not get re-derived.

name: ESP05_bool_demux
comment: PROVED. Demultiplexes the eight ESP_05 (0x106) booleans packed in ECD_esp05_bool_stage -- read through its context copy d000a60a -- into the 0xd00000xx/0xd00001xx config-bit block. THE ECD ARROW: 0x800a5b12 jz.t d15,#0x5 -> 0x800a5b14 st.t 0xd0000179,#0x5,#0x1 / 0x800a5b1a st.t 0xd0000179,#0x5,#0x0. No inversion, so d0000179 bit 5 = d000a60a bit 5 = ESP_05 frame bit 33 = ECD_nicht_verfuegbar. Sibling arrows in the same block: a60a b0->d00000ae b2, b4->d00000f9 b5, b2->d00000e4 b4, b3->d00000f2 b5, b7->d000011c b7, and b6->d000017a b7 for param_1==0x3c only. The demux runs only when FUN_800a06f2(...) returns 0 (signal valid); when it returns non-zero and != 3 the function FORCE-SETS d0000179 bit 5 at 0x800a5b64. That fail-safe direction (RX loss => ECD declared UNAVAILABLE) is what fixes the polarity beyond argument: bit set = unavailable.

name: ECD_unavail_powerup_forcer
comment: PROVED. Initialiser that force-sets d0000179 bit 5 = 1 at 0x800a5756 (st.t 0xd0000179,#0x5,#0x1) -- the ECU boots with ECD declared UNAVAILABLE until ESP_05 says otherwise. Together with the substitution force-set at 0x800a5b64 and the set/clear pair at 0x800a5b14/1a in ESP05_bool_demux, these are the ONLY writers of that bit anywhere: enumerated over all 6406 functions with core/ghidra/FindEffectiveAddr.java, which is ABS-mode aware (the pre-2026-08 tool could not see st.t at all, which is how this whole family was previously missed).

name: ECD_cfgbit_mirror_A
comment: PROVED. First of three cycle-rate ABS-mode mirror engines that copy d0000179 bit 5 into d000017a bit 4: 0x80313e4a ld.bu d15,0xd0000179; 0x80313e4e jz.t d15,#0x5; 0x80313e52 st.t 0xd000017a,#0x4,#0x1 / 0x80313e58 st.t 0xd000017a,#0x4,#0x0. No inversion, so d000017a bit 4 SET = ECD unavailable. The same three functions mirror d0000147 b4 and d00000f2 b5 in adjacent blocks. These writes are what falsified the old claim that d000017a is static variant coding.

name: ECD_cfgbit_mirror_B
comment: PROVED. Second cycle-rate mirror of d0000179 bit 5 -> d000017a bit 4: test 0x8031530e/12, set 0x80315316, clear 0x8031531c. Identical in shape to ECD_cfgbit_mirror_A (0x80313d20); which of the three runs is context/state dependent and was not resolved -- for the ECD trace it does not matter, all three compute the same function.

name: ECD_cfgbit_mirror_C
comment: PROVED. Third cycle-rate mirror of d0000179 bit 5 -> d000017a bit 4: test 0x80316422/26, set 0x8031642a, clear 0x80316430. See 0x80313d20.

name: ESP05_ctx_shadow_restore
comment: PROVED. The FORWARD copy on the ECD relay path: 0x80318152 ld.bu from 0xd000ab42 (lea a15,[a0]-0x18de) then 0x80318158 st.b to 0xd000a60a (lea a15,[a0]-0x1e16), a0 = 0xd000c420. Two identical siblings do the same store: FUN_8031896c @0x80318c0a and FUN_80319250 @0x803194ee. Those three plus COM_rx_default_substitution @0x8008b24c (orn d15,d15,#0x7f -- sets only bit 7 on RX timeout, never bit 5) are the ONLY writers of d000a60a in 6406 functions per core/ghidra/FindEffectiveAddr.java storesOnly.

name: ESP05_ctx_shadow_restore_B
comment: PROVED. Second of three identical ab42 -> a60a copiers on the ECD relay path; the store is 0x80318c0a. See 0x80317ea8.

name: ESP05_ctx_shadow_restore_C
comment: PROVED. Third of three identical ab42 -> a60a copiers on the ECD relay path; the store is 0x803194ee. See 0x80317ea8.

name: ESP05_ctx_shadow_save
comment: PROVED, AND THE DIRECTION MATTERS. This is the SAVE half of the ESP_05 staging pair: 0x80316f5c lea a15,[a0]-0x1e16 (=d000a60a), 0x80316f60 ld.bu, 0x80316f62 lea a15,[a0]-0x18de (=d000ab42), 0x80316f66 st.b -- i.e. ab42 = a60a, the REVERSE of the ECD forward path. It is the same circular write-back pattern as d000a6c7/d000ab6a, which is why a naive writer enumeration on either byte looks like it has no originator (the originator is the COM boolean unpacker storing through a descriptor pointer, so it leaves no static reference). NOTE: ecus/med17/maps/ecd_relay.md cites 0x80316f60/66 for the ab42 -> a60a step; that citation is backwards -- the forward copy is 0x80318152/58 (see 0x80317ea8).

name: ACC_abort_request_guard
comment: *** THE JOIN BETWEEN THE ECD RELAY AND THE ENGAGE STATE MACHINE -- this is the common flag the on-car data implies. *** Four instructions: 0x80143b2a ld.bu d2,[a15]0xb1 with a15 = 0xd0004918, i.e. d00049c9 = ACC_abort_request, then ne d2,d2,#0. It returns (whole byte != 0), so BIT 2 ALONE -- which is the ECD-unavailable term -- is sufficient to abort. Called from five sites in ACC_engage_state_machine@0x80143b8a: cases 1, 2 and 5 (true => FUN_80143954 then ACC_engage_state = 0), and case 3 + the default engage evaluation (true => the re-engage chain is blocked). PROVED from the decompiled control flow of 0x80143b8a plus the disassembly of the guard. This single byte is why TSK_01 frame bit 23, TSK_04 TSK_Status_GRA_ACC_02, TSK_04 TSK_ax_Getriebe and TSK_02 TSK_Verzoeg_Anf all move together: bit 2 is BOTH transmitted (as frame bit 23) and consumed (as the abort).

name: TSK04_producer
comment: *** ON THIS CALIBRATION THIS FUNCTION IS A SEVEN-LINE COPIER AND ITS ENTIRE LONG BODY IS DEAD CODE. *** PROVED: the head test at 0x801455ae-0x801455c0 is `if ((cal_obj(a9+0x3ec)[0x21] == 0 && cal_obj(a9+0x3ec)[0x24] == 0) || a454 != 2) -> short branch`. cal_obj(a9+0x3ec) = 0x803b5230 and BOTH bytes are zero in the image (0x803b5251 = 0, 0x803b5254 = 0), so the short branch is taken UNCONDITIONALLY regardless of a454. Short branch, every store read off the disassembly: d000ab03 = d000a35f; d000a361 = ACC_regulating_a362; **d000ab01 = ACC_status_a350 (load 0x801455e4, store 0x801455ee)**; d0005f20 = d0005cdc; d0005d00 = d0005d04; d000ab02 = d000a354; d0005f24 = d0005ce8; ret at 0x80145610. CONSEQUENCE: TSK_04 TSK_Status_GRA_ACC_02 (62|2, descriptor 0x80039208) is a DIRECT COPY of the engage state machine's d0004936, so an ECD abort rails it in the same transition that rails the accel and decel channels -- which is exactly the measured lockstep. The long body (a368-derived status, the DSM fault word, the case 0-3 switch, the d0000121-bit-5 suppressor) never executes here; do not reason from it.

name: ACC_engage_abort_reset
comment: PROVED from the decompile. Abort/exit routine of ACC_engage_state_machine, called from cases 1, 2 and 5 immediately before ACC_engage_state = 0 -- i.e. this is what runs the moment ACC_abort_request_guard reports the ECD bit. It writes d0004941 = 0 (-> ACC_regulating_a362 = 0), d000493f = 1, d000493e = 0, and snapshots the ramp state (d0004a38/a40/a42/a2c/a20). It does NOT zero d0004936; that happens one cycle later in ACC_engage_disengage_reset@0x801439fc. That one-to-two-cycle settle is the static counterpart of the on-car observation that all 81 frames with non-zero TSK_Verzoeg_Anf while ECD is unavailable lie inside a 200 ms window around an edge.

name: ACC_engage_disengage_reset
comment: PROVED from the decompile. The disengage reset run every cycle in ACC_engage_state_machine's default and case-3 paths. Its first two stores are d0004936 = 0 and d0004941 = 0, i.e. ACC_status_a350 and ACC_regulating_a362 go to zero TOGETHER in one transition. THAT is the mechanism behind the measured lockstep: a350 -> TSK_04 status (via TSK04_producer's short branch) and -> TSK_ax_Getriebe (via the bVar11 gate in TSK_status_coordinator), a362 -> TSK_Verzoeg_Anf (via TSK02_decel_gate). Also clears d0004a68, d000f82f, d00049cb, d0004921.

name: ACC_engage_a346_guard
comment: PROVED. Three-instruction guard returning ((d0004930 & 3) == 1) -- the low two bits of the TSK_status_shadow_a346 snapshot. Called in ACC_engage_state_machine case 3 and default as a re-engage precondition. SECOND-ORDER ECD EFFECT: those two bits are built in TSK02_producer at 0x80140cbe-0x80140cf4 from the SAME (d000017a bit 4 && d000a14d) term as a346 bit 5 -- they read 0 when ECD is unavailable-confirmed, 2 when ECD is available, and 1 only via the separate d000ab0f / d00000cd branch. Recorded so the a346 low bits are not mistaken for an independent input. The first-order block is ACC_abort_request_guard.

name: ACC_engage_fault_abort_guard
comment: PROVED from the decompile. First guard evaluated in ACC_engage_state_machine cases 1, 2, 5, 6 and default; returns 1 (abort) if d000492e == 3, or DSM_get_event_status(*(0x80028bb8)) == 0, or (d0004930 & 0x10) != 0. Its d0004930 BIT 4 term is a DSM lock carried through TSK_status_shadow_a346 bit 4 -- NOT the ECD bit, which is bit 5 of the same snapshot byte. Recorded because the two adjacent bits of one byte reach the state machine through two different guards and are easy to conflate.

name: ECD_esp05_bool_stage
comment: PROVED. COM staging byte holding EIGHT ESP_05 (CAN 0x106) booleans, written by the generated COM boolean unpacker through 20-byte descriptors 0x800346f8 / 470c / 4720 / 4748 / 4770 / **4784** / 4798 / 484c -- all inside ESP_05's own 19-record descriptor run at 0x800346e4..0x8003485c, which message record 0x80031718 declares explicitly (n_bool = 19). **BIT 5 = ESP_05 frame bit 33 = ECD_nicht_verfuegbar** (descriptor 0x80034784: srcBit 0x21 = 33, destBit 0x05). This is the entry point of the entire measured 15 km/h ACC floor. Other bits: b7<-srcBit 13, b3<-26, b0<-27, b4<-29, b6<-32, b1<-34, b2<-61. Only ONE static writer exists in the image (ESP05_ctx_shadow_save @0x80316f66, which copies d000a60a BACK into it); the real producer stores through a descriptor pointer and therefore leaves no reference -- do NOT read the empty writer list as evidence of no producer.

name: ECD_unavail_cfg179
comment: PROVED. Config-bit byte whose BIT 5 is `ECD not available`, demuxed from ECD_esp05_bool_stage via the context copy d000a60a. Writers of bit 5, enumerated exhaustively over 6406 functions with the ABS-aware core/ghidra/FindEffectiveAddr.java: 0x800a5b14 (set) and 0x800a5b1a (clear) in ESP05_bool_demux, 0x800a5b64 (force-set on the RX-substitution path), and 0x800a5756 (force-set at init). No other writer; no inversion anywhere. The other seven bits belong to unrelated subsystems (b0<-802d0e66, b1<-800690ec, b2<-80052bf0, b3<-80193c74, b4<-8016fee4/801705b8, b6<-802c68a6, b7<-80063c04) -- listing them matters because a byte-granular trace of this address would otherwise pick up eleven irrelevant writers.

name: ECD_unavail_prev_cycle
comment: PROVED. One-cycle delay memory for the ECD bit. SOLE writer image-wide is 0x80140d4a in TSK02_producer: `lea a15,[a0]-0x22d3 (=0xd000a14d); ld.bu d15,0xd000017a; extr.u d15,d15,#0x4,#0x1; st.b [a15]#0x0,d15` -- so it holds d000017a bit 4 as of the END of the previous TSK_02 cycle. It is READ earlier in the same function, at 0x80140b9a (condition vector bit 0) and 0x80140cec (the a346 low-bits branch), so EVERY ECD test in this ECU is the two-sample AND (b4_now && b4_prev). This is the ECU-internal source of one extra cycle of SET-edge delay, with none on release -- the same asymmetry direction the on-car lag analysis measures.

name: TSK_ACC_snapshot_4930
comment: PROVED. Entry-block snapshot of TSK_status_shadow_a346 taken by TSK_status_coordinator: 0x80144830 lea a15,[a0]-0x20da (= 0xd000a346), 0x80144840 ld.bu, 0x80144846 st.b [a12]0x18 with a12 = 0xd0004918. Bit layout inherited from a346: bits 1:0 = the 0/1/2 ECD-derived state, bit 4 = a DSM lock, **bit 5 = the ECD-unavailable term**. Consumers: 0x80144cdc ld.bu -> 0x80144ce4 extr.u d9,d15,#0x5,#0x1 -> TSK_bool_packer slot 2 -> ACC_abort_request bit 2; ACC_engage_fault_abort_guard (bit 4); ACC_engage_a346_guard (bits 1:0); and (d0004930 & 3) == 2 inside ACC_engage_state_machine case 1.

name: TSK01_status_word
comment: PROVED, AND IT CLOSES THE LAST INFERRED LINK IN THE OLD CHAIN. The 24-bit TSK_01 (0x10A) TSK_Status_AB word, assembled in TSK_status_coordinator and stored at 0x801450e6 (st.w [a0]-0x7ae8). Built from three TSK_bool_packer bytes: packer@0x80144fb4 -> bits 0-7, packer@0x80145054 -> bits 8-15 (sha d2,d2,#0x8 at 0x80145062), packer@0x801450a0 -> bits 16-23 (sha #0x10 at 0x801450a8), OR-ed at 0x80145070 / 0x801450b6 and then OR-ed with the two stretch latches at 0x801450c0 / 0x801450d8 / 0x801450e4. **BIT 7 = ACC_abort_request bit 2 = ECD unavailable**: 0x80144f9a ld.bu d15,[a15]0xb1 (= d00049c9), 0x80144fa4 extr.u d15,d15,#0x2,#0x1, 0x80144fac st.w [a10]#0xc -- and TSK_bool_packer maps [a10]+0x0c to bit 7. Since TSK_01's descriptor 0x80039460 places this word at start_bit 16 len 24 and COM packing is LSB-first, word bit 7 = FRAME BIT 23. The byte-to-frame attribution is now taken from the descriptor, not derived by elimination as the old d000f82a row had to do.

name: TSK01_status_stage
comment: PROVED. Intermediate copy of TSK01_status_word: TSK_status_coordinator does d0005e38 = d0004938 at 0x801453e6 (ld.w [a0]-0x7ae8) / 0x801453ee (st.w [a0]-0x65e8). Later, 0x801454a4 reloads it, 0x801454ac conditionally does `andn d15,d0,#0x3c` (clearing bits 2-5 only, under a d0004a7c dwell timer over cal_obj(a9+0x3e8)+0x50 = 30), 0x801454b0 writes it back and 0x801454b6 stores the result to TSK01_StatusAB_tx (d0005e34). The andn mask does not include bit 7, so the ECD bit reaches frame bit 23 unmodified.

name: TSK01_status_stretch_lat0
comment: PROVED. First stage of the two-deep shift register that STRETCHES selected TSK_01 status bits. 0x801450d0 ld.w [a2]#0x4 (= cal 0x803dc15c) and 0x801450d2 `and d15,d2` mask the fresh 24-bit vector; 0x801450dc stores the masked value here (st.w [a0]-0x7a5c). Read back one cycle later at 0x801450bc and OR-ed into the outgoing word, then shifted into TSK01_status_stretch_lat1 at 0x801450c8. Bit 7 is in the mask, so the ECD-derived abort bit is held asserted for two extra 20 ms cycles in TSK_01 frame bit 23 after ACC_abort_request bit 2 clears.

name: TSK01_status_stretch_lat1
comment: PROVED. Second stage of the TSK_01 status stretch shift register: read at 0x801450a4 (ld.w [a0]-0x7a64), OR-ed into the outgoing word at 0x801450c0, and reloaded from TSK01_status_stretch_lat0 at 0x801450c8. Together with 0xd00049c4 it gives the masked bits a minimum three-cycle assertion. Also mirrored to the telemetry shadows d000f820 / d00049c0 at 0x801450b0 / 0x801450b8.

name: C_TSK01_status_stretch_mask
comment: READ FROM THE IMAGE, not assumed: cal_obj(a9+0xc40) = 0x803dc158, so this is +0x04, value 0x000040c2. It is the 24-bit selection mask for the TSK_01 status stretch latches, applied at 0x801450d0/d2. Set bits are 1, 6, 7 and 14. **Bit 7 is set**, so the ECD-derived abort bit in TSK_01 frame bit 23 is held for two extra cycles after its source clears. This is the only calibratable timing element on the TSK_01 leg of the ECD path.

name: C_ECD_condvec_select_mask
comment: *** THE ONE CALIBRATION BYTE THAT WIRES ECD INTO THE ACC ABORT. *** cal_obj(a9+0xc30) = 0x803dba70, so this is +0x0d; value read from the image = 0x01. Applied at 0x80140d0a in TSK02_producer (`ld.a a15,[a9]0xc30; ld.bu d15,[a15]#0xd; and d15,d13`) to an 8-bit condition vector, and the result becomes TSK_status_shadow_a346 bit 5 via 0x80140d10 `insert d15,d9,d8,#0x5,#0x1`. Value 0x01 selects condition-vector BIT 0 ONLY, and bit 0 is built at 0x80140b8c-0x80140ba0 as (d000017a bit 4 && d000a14d) = ECD unavailable, confirmed over two cycles. The other seven vector bits (d000ab00 state compares at 0x80140ba8-0x80140bfa, three DSM paths at 0x80140c02/c22/c42, and a segment-0xC debounce at 0x80140caa) are masked out. LEVER, UNTESTED: 0x01 -> 0x00 severs ECD -> a346 bit 5 -> abort request at this point, but does NOT sever the parallel use of the same term at 0x80140ce0-0x80140cf4 (a346 bits 1:0), and of course does not make the ESP grant ECD.

name: C_ACC_abort_request_mask
comment: READ FROM THE IMAGE: cal_obj(a9+0x3e8) = 0x803b5088, so this is +0x37, value 0xFF. AND-mask applied to the TSK_bool_packer output at 0x80144d56/5a before it is stored to d000f829 (0x80144d5c), ACC_abort_request d00049c9 (0x80144d62) and d0004933 (0x80144d66). 0xFF passes everything, so BIT 2 -- the ECD term, packer slot 2 fed from d0004930 bit 5 -- reaches the abort request unmodified. **CANDIDATE LEVER: 0xFF -> 0xFB.** That clears bit 2 and would remove the ECD-driven ACC abort at the consumer while simultaneously clearing TSK_01 frame bit 23. It does NOT make the ESP grant ECD, so the brake-side decel request would still be refused; it only stops the ENGINE disengaging on the declaration. Needs a cal-block checksum recompute (core/checksum). CAUTION: the other seven bits are independent live abort reasons.

name: ACC_engage_status_raw
comment: PROVED. ACC_engage_state_machine's status output. Copied verbatim to ACC_status_a350 by TSK_status_coordinator at 0x801453d6 (ld.bu d15,[a12]0x1e) / 0x801453de (st.b [a13] with a13 = 0xd000a350). Values 0 = disengaged, 1 and 2 = engaged variants, 3 = fault. ZEROED by ACC_engage_disengage_reset@0x801439fc together with d0004941. Because TSK04_producer takes its short branch on this calibration, a350 IS TSK_04 TSK_Status_GRA_ACC_02 -- so this byte is simultaneously the TSK_04 status on the wire and the gate term for TSK_ax_Getriebe.

name: ACC_regulating_raw
comment: PROVED (decompile plus operand order in the disassembly). ACC_engage_state_machine's actively-regulating output; copied to ACC_regulating_a362 at 0x801453ce (ld.bu d15,[a12]0x29) / 0x801453d4 (st.b through an address register loaded from d8, which is why core/ghidra/FindEffectiveAddr.java cannot resolve this particular store -- the decompile shows it plainly as `ACC_regulating_a362 = DAT_d0004941`). Set to 1/2/5 while engaged; zeroed by ACC_engage_disengage_reset@0x801439fc and by ACC_engage_abort_reset@0x80143954; set to 4 in state 6.

name: ACC_engage_hold_flag_raw
comment: PROVED. State-machine flag copied to d000a356 at 0x801453e0/e4. It is the SECOND term of TSK02_decel_gate's regulating test ((a362 in {1,5}) || a356 != 0), so it governs HOW FAST TSK_Verzoeg_Anf collapses after an ECD abort rather than whether it does. ACC_engage_abort_reset@0x80143954 SETS it to 1 on the abort cycle; the case-3 path clears it to 0 one to two cycles later, after which the decel request is hard-zeroed. That is the static counterpart of the 81 out-of-window frames in the on-car ECD analysis, all of which fall inside a 200 ms edge window.

name: ACC_engage_hold_flag
comment: PROVED. = d000493f, written by TSK_status_coordinator at 0x801453e4. Read by TSK02_decel_gate as the alternative to (a362 in {1,5}) in the gate that admits TSK_decel_request_value to TSK_Verzoeg_Anf_tx. See 0xd000493f for why it matters to the edge timing rather than the steady state.

name: TSK_decel_request_value
comment: PROVED. The decel-request magnitude handed from the ACC controller to the TSK_02 transmitter: TSK_status_coordinator writes d00082c0 = d000491a. TSK02_decel_gate then transmits `uVar8 = 0; if (bVar1) uVar8 = d00082c0;` into TSK_Verzoeg_Anf_tx (d0008d5a). Note the substitution is a LITERAL ZERO, not a calibration -- which is why this signal's neutral on the wire is raw 166 = 0.000 m/s^2 while TSK_ax_Getriebe's neutral comes from cal 0x803b508a.

name: TSK02_decel_permit_latch
comment: PROVED from the decompile. Latch inside TSK02_decel_gate that carries the decel permit between cycles. It is set to 1 only while bVar5 (the regulating test AND d0005cb0 <= d0005cc0 AND d000a363 == 0) is true, and forced to 0 whenever bVar2 is true. The transmitted gate is (bVar5 || d0002a02), so this latch is the ONLY element that could delay TSK_Verzoeg_Anf reaching zero after an ECD abort; bVar2 goes true as soon as the regulating terms clear, bounding the delay at one to two cycles. INFERRED (not measured): this is the mechanism behind the 81 non-zero frames inside the 200 ms propagation window.

name: TSK02_bit54_from_a350
comment: PROVED for the binding and the writer; the SIGNAL NAME is NOT asserted. TSK_02 (0x10C) frame bit 54 -- COM boolean descriptor 0x80034ba8 (srcBit 54, destBit 0) inside 0x10C's declared 6-record run at 0x80034b58 (message record 0x80031418, n_bool = 6); the same RAM byte is also bound to CAN 0x111 bit 54 via descriptor 0x80034b08. Sole writer is the TSK02_decel_gate tail: d000a345 = (ACC_status_a350 in {1,2}) && (bVar18 || a454 == 2). So this is a THIRD TSK_02 output railed by the same ECD abort -- when ACC_engage_disengage_reset zeroes d0004936, this bit clears too.

name: TSK02_bit12_from_a362
comment: PROVED for the binding and the writer; the SIGNAL NAME is NOT asserted, and it CONTRADICTS an existing map. TSK_02 (0x10C) frame bit 12 -- COM boolean descriptor 0x80034b58 (srcBit 12, destBit 0), the first record of 0x10C's declared 6-record run. Sole writer is the TSK02_decel_gate tail: d000a33d = ((a362 in {1,5}) && a454 == 2) ? (d0000113 bit 4) : 0 -- a FOURTH TSK_02 output railed by the ECD abort. CONFLICT: ecus/med17/maps/acc_flow.md attributes 0x10C 12|1 (TSK_Anhalten in the DBC geometry) to d000a35c. That attribution came from the OLD off-by-one boolean table; the corrected table binds bit 12 here. Flagged, not renamed -- the DBC identity of the bit was not re-verified in this pass.

name: ACC_mode_a454
comment: PROVED as the outermost gate on all four TSK producers, so it is the boundary condition on the entire ECD relay. TSK02_producer forces TSK_status_shadow_a346 to 0 unless (a454 == 2) or (a454 == 1 and d000a7e8 bit 1) -- which would zero the ECD term and hence TSK_01 frame bit 23. TSK_status_coordinator requires a454 in {1,2} for the TSK_ax_Getriebe gate bVar11. TSK02_decel_gate returns early unless a454 == 2, or == 1 with d000a7e8 bit 1. TSK04_producer tests it but the test is irrelevant here (see 0x801455ae). Fed from ACC_master_mode (d000a3c1) via FUN_802c806e. Check a454 == 2 before trusting any part of the relay trace.

name: C_TSK_ax_Getriebe_neutral
comment: READ FROM THE IMAGE: cal_obj(a9+0x3e8) = 0x803b5088, so this is +0x02, value 0. The substitute written to TSK_ax_Getriebe_tx (d00082b6, TSK_04 18|9) whenever the accel gate is false -- which is exactly what an ECD abort causes, because the gate is bVar11 = (a454 in {1,2}) && (a350 == 1 || (a350 == 2 && cal_obj(a9+0x3e8)[0x41] != 0)), and 0x803b50c9 = 1 on this image, so effectively a350 in {1,2}. Packs to wire raw 84 = +0.000 m/s^2, matching the measured neutral. PROVED that the ECD abort reaches this substitution: abort -> ACC_engage_disengage_reset zeroes d0004936 -> a350 = 0 -> gate false.

name: C_TSK04_longpath_enable_A
comment: READ FROM THE IMAGE: cal_obj(a9+0x3ec) = 0x803b5230, so this is +0x21, value 0. First of the two enable bytes that select TSK04_producer's long body; tested at 0x801455b6 (ld.bu d15,[a15]0x21; jnz). With this AND 0x803b5254 both zero, FUN_801455ae takes its seven-line short branch unconditionally, so TSK_04 TSK_Status_GRA_ACC_02 = ACC_status_a350 and the whole a368/DSM/case-switch body is dead code on this image. Recorded because anyone reading FUN_801455ae top to bottom will otherwise model TSK_04 completely wrongly -- as this project did.

name: C_TSK04_longpath_enable_B
comment: READ FROM THE IMAGE: cal_obj(a9+0x3ec)+0x24 = 0x803b5230+0x24, value 0. Second enable byte for TSK04_producer's long body, tested at 0x801455bc (ld.bu d15,[a15]0x24; jz -> short branch). See 0x803b5251.

name: COM_bool_desc_ECD_unavail
comment: *** THE DESCRIPTOR THAT MAKES THE 15 km/h FLOOR EXTERNAL. *** 20-byte COM boolean descriptor: word0 = 0xd000ab42 (target), word1 = 0xffff0521 -> srcBit 0x21 = 33, destBit 0x05, callback (+0x0c) = 0x800286c6. It lands ESP_05 frame bit 33 (ECD_nicht_verfuegbar) in ECD_esp05_bool_stage bit 5. OWNERSHIP PROVED, not inferred: message record 0x80031718 (CAN 0x106) declares n_bool = 19 at +0x01 and firstBool = 0x800346e4 at +0x04, and 0x800346e4 + 19*0x14 = 0x80034860, which is EXACTLY the firstBool of the next record (0x101 @0x800316e8) -- the runs tile the table with no slack, so the attribution is self-checking rather than assumed.

name: COM_bool_run_ESP_05
comment: PROVED. Start of ESP_05's (CAN 0x106) 19-record boolean-descriptor run: 0x800346e4..0x8003485c inclusive, stride 0x14, declared by message record 0x80031718 fields +0x01 (n_bool = 19) and +0x04 (pointer). Contains the ECD entry (0x80034784, srcBit 33 -> d000ab42 b5) and the hill-descent entry (0x800347ac, srcBit 36 -> d000ab6a). Recorded explicitly because the previous decode read this pointer at the wrong offset from the wrong base and shifted every boolean binding by one message, which is what made ESP_05 bit 33 look like a CAN 0x101 bit and sent this project hunting a non-existent internal threshold.

name: CAN_0x106_ESP_05
comment: ESP_05 message record, record 58 of the corrected CAN message table (base 0x80030c38, stride 0x30, 113 records). Fields: +0x01 n_bool = 19, +0x02 n_sig = 6, +0x04 firstBool = 0x800346e4, +0x08 sigBlock = 0x80032dd4, +0x0c id = 0x106. *** THIS SUPERSEDES the row at 0x80031720, which was this same record read at the WRONG BASE and which concluded the ECU never unpacks bit 33. It does. *** The old row was right that ESP_05's six MULTI-BIT signals (descriptors 0x80038588..0x80038650, start_bits 0/8/14/16/42/48) do not include bit 33; its error was assuming the signal table was the whole story and reading the boolean pointer one record late. Boolean descriptor 0x80034784 binds frame bit 33 to d000ab42 bit 5, and the relay is instruction-proven from there to TSK_01, TSK_02 and TSK_04.

name: CAN_0x111_TSK_05
comment: CAN 0x111 message record (base 0x80030c38 table). Recorded because its signal and boolean blocks RE-USE the same RAM as TSK_02: d0008d5a at 56|8 (descriptor 0x800390c8), d000ab01 at 16|2 (descriptor 0x80039190), and the same three booleans d000a358 / d000a33f / d000a345 at srcBits 23 / 53 / 54 (descriptors 0x80034ae0 / af4 / b08). CONSEQUENCE: every effect of an ECD abort on TSK_02 appears identically on 0x111 if that message is transmitted on this vehicle. NOT checked against the on-car log in this pass -- flagged so nobody concludes a TSK_02 RAM byte has exactly one message binding.
